\subsection{T4 -- Transactional bursts}
Executed on 2026-10-21 (09:05--09:26 CEST) with the state-changing
operation \texttt{RegisterProduction} and 32 client connections. Submission schedules were precomputed and
saved with their seed (20261021); requests are released open-loop at their scheduled offsets.
Profile~A releases $B$ requests at the same instant; profile~B releases 50 requests every 5\,s for
60\,s (inter-burst interval 5\,s, burst duration $\approx$0\,s); profile~C draws exponential
inter-arrival times with mean rates 80 and 128\,TPS over 60\,s
(approximately 50\% and 80\% of the maximum sustainable state-changing rate measured in T2). Each configuration was
repeated 5 times with 10\,s of idle time between runs. Completion time is measured from the first
submission to the last commit of the run.

\paragraph{Observations.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Correctness under bursts.} 67113 of 67113 requests were committed as valid
        (0 invalid or unresolved).
  \item \textbf{Burst absorption.} Single bursts of 10, 50, 100, 200 requests (released within at most 118.7\,ms) were completed in 0.09\,s, 0.27\,s, 0.43\,s, 0.80\,s respectively, from the first submission to the last commit, with P95 latencies of 90, 260, 418, 749\,ms. In the periodic profile, 60 of 60 bursts were fully committed before the next burst was released (maximum burst completion time 0.28\,s), so no backlog accumulated between bursts.
  \item \textbf{Random arrivals.} Under Poisson arrivals (79.6\,TPS achieved, inter-arrival CV 1.00; 128.1\,TPS achieved, inter-arrival CV 0.99) the P95 latency was 183\,ms and 131\,ms and the number of outstanding requests stayed below 22 and 43 respectively.
  \item \textbf{Batching effect.} Larger bursts fill blocks of \texttt{MaxMessageCount} = 10 transactions immediately,
        so the latency of a burst is driven by the number of blocks to be cut and committed rather than by the
        2\,s \texttt{BatchTimeout}.
\end{itemize}
